searchText: I agree, i'd would go so far as to say we should consider dropping it in the future. It complicates things and confuses users. will be tricky with eip-1271 esp. given smart contracts can invalidate signatures I'm not sure 0x01 credentials would be given new rights in the future as that might break a security promise of today, but an extended 0x02 following something akin to dankrad's proposal might make sense. That said, arbitrary communication/signal from application layer to the beacon chain has complexity and overhead that needs to be considered I'm not talking about communications from the application layer to the beacon chain, I'm talking about a future beacon chain operation that may be signed with the BLS withdrawal key. If we can have an assurance that 0x01 credentials can sign any such operations that would pave the way to use 0x01 credentials for future deposits. 0x01 can be a smart contract in the application layer so you would have to effectively communicate something across this layer, right? This is more for EOAs than smart contracts. Basically thinking about using them as a drop-in replacement for BLS keys. Stated differently, The main use case of 0x00 creds today seems to be as an intermediate state b/w staking and eoa eth1 addresses. So why not just use eoa 0x01 creds in those cases?
